title: Miriam P NDE 3846
content: The surgery was scheduled for afternoon, they laid me on the operating table and the anesthesiologist gave me the anesthesia, I saw that other people entered the operating room I think they were nurses and nurses' aides. At that moment, I wasn't looking at the doctor. What I remember is being conscious and wanting to open my eyes and move my body because I heard the monitors going off and the doctor saying that they had lost me. The doctor asked a woman if my husband was outside. He told her to go speak with my husband. The aide asked, 'What's going on? The doctor said, 'Sew her up.' I wanted to scream and tell them that I was still here but I couldn't open my eyes. It seemed as though there were fractions of a second in which I saw scenes of my life with my family, my children, my husband and my work colleagues and I asked myself why, since there was so much more for me to do, when the most beautiful music surrounded me and I resigned myself to staying. Then I saw my twenty-year-old son leaning against a wall. My sister-in-law was asking him how my husband was doing. He answered, 'He's better now.' Then I realized that hours had passed. I heard my other son. He was walking and they had already told him about my death. I was sad thinking about the pain that my death was causing everybody and I said to myself that I needed to go back, it wasn't fair even if the peace and serenity that I was feeling was so wonderful and unexplainable. I felt a pain in my chest. It was starting up slowly until it built into a terrible pain. I said to myself, 'it doesn't matter if it hurts. I have to go back.' In that moment, it was as if the same movie that I had just seen began, started to go in reverse. I heard them tell the aide that I had returned and a moment later the nurse told me they were taking me to a hospital room. I believe I was conscious throughout the whole event and the most significant part is the cycle of life. The next day I asked the doctor what had happened and he simply said that I had not taken the anesthesia well.

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: Return was described as 'as if the same movie that I had just seen began...to go in reverse.'

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Auditory awareness of operating room staff and monitors; perceived observation of family members after being told she had died; 'most beautiful music' surrounding her; reverse 'movie' during return.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Experience emphasized awareness during surgery, brief life scenes, perceived later family scenes, then a chosen return described as a reverse replay.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Return described as a 'movie' reversing; strong auditory awareness during anesthesia with inability to move; 'most beautiful music' surrounding her; perceived scenes of family occurring hours later.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “I heard the monitors going off and the doctor saying that they had lost me.” “Sew her up.” “it wasn't fair even if the peace and serenity that I was feeling was so wonderful and unexplainable.” “In that moment, it was as if the same movie that I had just seen began, started to go in reverse.”
